subject: science
passage: Saturn's rings look solid from a distance, but they are made of countless separate pieces. The particles that make up the ring system, each following its own orbit around the planet, ______ composed overwhelmingly of water ice, which is why the rings reflect so much sunlight. Measurements of the rings' mass by the Cassini spacecraft have led some scientists to propose that the rings formed within the last few hundred million years, although others argue that the rings could be far older and have simply been kept clean of darker dust.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject of the verb is "The particles," which is plural. "That make up the ring system" and "each following its own orbit around the planet" both describe the particles, and the singular words inside them ("system," "each," "its") do not change the subject. A plural subject needs the plural verb "are," which also fits the present-tense description.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Is" is singular and seems to agree with "system" or "each," but the subject is the plural "particles."
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Has been" is singular, but the subject "particles" is plural.
explanation.C: Correct. The plural verb "are" agrees with the plural subject "The particles."
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Was" is singular, and its past tense also clashes with the present-tense description; the subject "particles" is plural.
